definitions.explanation: A feeling of being fed up with or thoroughly tired of something, leading to a desire to avoid it.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}に{嫌気|いやけ}がさした。
examples.english: I got fed up with work.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}の{残業|ざんぎょう}に{嫌気|いやけ}がさしている。
examples.english: I'm fed up with the daily overtime.

examples.japanese: {人間関係|にんげんかんけい}に{嫌気|いやけ}がさして、{田舎|いなか}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}した。
examples.english: I grew so tired of human relationships that I moved to the countryside.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
{嫌|いや} (unpleasant, disagreeable) + {気|け} (feeling, sense)

KEY PATTERN:
Almost always used with がさす: {嫌気|いやけ}がさす (to become disgusted with, to grow tired of). The pattern ～に{嫌気|いやけ}がさす means "to get fed up with ~."

NUANCE:
Stronger than {飽|あ}きる (to get bored of). {嫌気|いやけ} implies not just loss of interest but active aversion or revulsion toward something that has become intolerable.

NOTE:
Do not confuse with {嫌気性|けんきせい} (anaerobic), where the reading is けんき.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {嫌気|いやけ}がさす: to get fed up, to feel disgusted
- ～に{嫌気|いやけ}がさす: to grow tired of ~
- {嫌気|いやけ}がさして: being fed up (as a reason)
